verdict.rationale: Poly ships its own built-in Monaco editor with keyboard-centric features (multiple cursors, find and replace, Vim keybindings, syntax highlighting), and journal entries are Markdown files that can have attachments. That covers the fast keyboard-driven editing and implies some formatting. Rich note formatting is not documented as a feature: there is no evidence of rendered headings, callouts, tables, code-block rendering or inline embedded media. missing for 10: documented headings/callouts/tables formatting, rendered code blocks in notes, embedded media within notes, independent or hands-on corroboration of editor speed.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can write and format notes with headings, callouts, tables, code blocks, and embedded media in a fast keyboard-driven editor

citations.quote: Poly includes a built-in Monaco editor... Syntax highlighting for dozens of languages, Find and replace, Multiple cursors, Vim keybindings
